title: This 150-Million-Year-Old Bird Had a Body Built for the Land - Nautilus
author: David Nield
text: Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisementPaleontologyThis 150-Million-Year-Old Bird Had a Body Built for the LandThe find indicates that flight may have evolved multiple timesDNBy David Nield7:00 AM CST on November 11, 2026Add Nautilus to GoogleLots of birds aren’t built for flight: chickens, penguins, emus, etc. This new species of bird (Yuezhuornis yangyuanensis), which lived around 150 million years ago, is another such odd duck (so to speak), though it boasts the added cachet of challenging the conventional understanding of bird evolution.Powered By 1020.6K 10ShareNextStayThe traditional view has been that natural selection prioritized characteristics that help birds fly across the millennia. But Yuezhuornis yangyuanensis had a body built more for living on land than in the air. For example, its fossil had sharp teeth, relatively short wings, and a claw on its foot for attacking predators. It’s very much like a small, predatory dinosaur, and experts believe it may not have been able to fly at all.And yet, it has bird-like features that put it firmly in the Avialae part of the animal kingdom—the evolutionary group where you’ll find modern birds and the extinct relatives closest to them.Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisement
